objectives: Build prefix sums and answer any range total in O(1).
Use a leading 0 so ranges that start at index 0 need no special case.
Turn questions about ranges into questions about pairs of prefix sums.

sections.heading: Intuition: a range is a difference of two running totals
paragraphs: The running total up to position r, minus the running total up to position l - 1, is the total of the range l..r. Everything before l cancels out. So if you store all running totals once, any range total is one subtraction.
Store them with a 0 in front: prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i] = the total of the first i values. Then the range l..r is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l], with no special case when l = 0.

callout.text: A question about a range l..r is a question about two prefix sums: prefix[r + 1] and prefix[l]. Once you see that, range problems become pair problems.

diagram.description: Prefix sums 0, 3, 1, 5 for values 3, -2, 4. The total of all three values is prefix[3] minus prefix[0].

sections.heading: Baseline: add up each range when asked
paragraphs: Adding the values in a range takes O(length). With many range questions on a long array, that's O(n) per question. Prefix sums take O(n) once and O(1) per question after that.

sections.heading: Worked example: range totals with prefix sums
paragraphs: For [3, -2, 4], the prefix sums are [0, 3, 1, 5]. The total of values 0 to 2 is prefix[3] - prefix[0] = 5. The total of values 1 to 2 is prefix[3] - prefix[1] = 2.
Negative values are fine: prefix sums don't have to increase. That's different from day 19's windows, which needed positive values.

sections.heading: Complexity and cautions
paragraphs: Building prefix sums takes O(n) time and O(n) memory. Each range query is O(1).
Prefix sums of many large values can overflow a 32-bit integer; use 64-bit totals in C++, Java, and Go.

sections.heading: Before you finish
paragraphs: Try to answer each question before opening it.

checks.prompt: Why start the prefix array with 0?
checks.answer: So the total of a range starting at index 0 is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[0], the same formula as every other range.

checks.prompt: What is the total of values[1..2] for [3, -2, 4]?
Why can't day 19's sliding window count subarrays with sum exactly k when values can be negative?
checks.answer: With negatives, growing a window can lower its sum and shrinking can raise it, so there's no single direction to move.
